        Hello! I am <strong>Geni</strong>, the intelligent assistant of <strong>GenoScribe</strong>.  
        I am here to help you interactively explore the content of this bioinformatics report.
      </p>

      <p>
        When you ask me a question, I first try to recognize whether it matches any of the patterns or expressions I know.  
        If I find a match, I will respond directly with a predefined answer, designed to be fast, clear, and even a bit witty.  
        If I do not recognize the pattern, I then activate my search tools: I generate vector representations (embeddings) and look for the most relevant fragments across multiple documents—including the report itself, external PDF and HTML files, and question-and-answer (QA) sessions.  
        Based on that information, I create a summary that aims to provide you with a coherent and useful response grounded in the existing content.
      </p>

      <p>
        Please note that this environment is experimental. I do not use large language models, so some responses may be approximate or incomplete.  
        The main goal is to provide a fast, understandable, and reproducible way to visualize the information contained in the documents, enabling a more dynamic exploration of the report.
      </p>

      <p>
        Currently, results may vary in accuracy, as I use lightweight local models to ensure the application runs in any environment without the need for external servers.  
        However, the system structure is designed to significantly improve its performance in the future through integration with more advanced models or external APIs.  
        To get started, simply type your question in the field below and let me take care of the rest. I promise to put all my code into it!
      </p>

<div class="titulo1" id="tab3-seccion6">
  6<span>.</span> Conclusions and perspectives
</div>

<p>
  Throughout this report, a comprehensive transcriptomic analysis has been conducted, covering all essential stages of the typical RNA-Seq gene expression workflow. 
  From the <strong>initial review of samples and their metadata</strong>, through <strong>quality control of raw reads</strong>, <strong>sequence alignment to the reference genome</strong>, and <strong>gene expression quantification</strong>, to the <strong>statistical and functional analysis of differentially expressed genes</strong>, each step has been implemented rigorously and reproducibly.
</p>

<p>
  The statistical analysis allowed the identification of <strong>genes whose expression is significantly altered</strong> between experimental conditions, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying observed phenotypes. 
  Through <strong>normalization</strong> procedures and <strong>post-alignment quality assessment</strong>, data reliability was ensured before applying robust inferential methodologies for the <strong>detection of differentially expressed genes (DEGs)</strong>.
</p>

<p>
  Finally, <strong>functional and enrichment analyses</strong> based on widely validated databases (GO and KEGG) enabled biological contextualization of the results, revealing <strong>biological processes, molecular functions, cellular components, and metabolic pathways</strong> potentially involved in the observed differential response. 
  This integration of information layers provides interpretative depth to the study and facilitates prioritization of genes and functions of interest for future experimental work.
</p>

<p>
  Overall, this report constitutes a valuable tool both for the <strong>initial exploration of transcriptomic data</strong> and for the <strong>formulation of new biological hypotheses</strong>. 
  The results obtained can guide decisions in subsequent phases of the project, such as the design of validation experiments or integration with other omics data sources.
</p>

<p>
  As a projection toward future directions, it is recommended:
</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Experimentally validate</strong> the most relevant genes using techniques such as RT-qPCR, Western blot, or in vitro/in vivo functional assays.
  </li>
  <li>
    Perform <strong>co-expression network analyses</strong> to identify potential key regulatory genes or coordinated functional modules.
  </li>
  <li>
    Explore <strong>multi-omics integration strategies</strong>, combining transcriptomic data with proteomic, epigenomic, or metabolomic information to achieve a more comprehensive view of the biological system.
  </li>
  <li>
    Implement <strong>advanced computational models</strong> (machine learning, Bayesian analysis, network modeling) to extract complex patterns and predict biological phenomena from the generated data.
  </li>
</ul>

<p>
  Overall, this analysis represents a fundamental step toward understanding the molecular mechanisms associated with the evaluated conditions, and lays the foundation for <strong>deeper and more targeted biomedical or biotechnological research</strong>.
</p>

<div class="titulo3" id="tab3-soporte">
  ➤ Support and Contact
</div>

<p>
  Bulk RNA-Seq transcriptomic analysis generates a vast and technically complex data ecosystem. We understand that digesting this information and integrating it with laboratory results is an ongoing process. 
</p>

<p>
  Therefore, for any methodological questions, inquiries about result interpretation, or the need to explore the data from new perspectives, the <strong>Bioinformatics Unit</strong> team is at your full disposal. We will be happy to assist you in the optimal use of this resource and in planning your future research directions.
</p>
